title: Wittmann wins the 2014 DTM opener at Hockenheim
dek: Marco Wittmann won the season opener at Hockenheim for BMW Team RMG by 12.869 seconds from Mattias Ekström, after passing pole-sitter Adrien Tambay early while Audi's standard-tyre starters charged late.

chapters.title: A new rulebook and a new BMW
text: The 2014 DTM season began at Hockenheim on Sunday 4 May, the first of ten races, and it came with a revised rulebook. Qualifying was cut from four sessions to three, with the fastest eight going into the final one for pole. The two mandatory pit stops of previous years became one, to be taken in the middle third of the race. The Hankook option tyre still had to be used once but for no more than half the distance, DRS could now be used right up to the flag, and the race was capped at 75 minutes. Every car also started the year with 10 kilograms of performance weight, which would move up or down by as much as 10 kilograms depending on how each manufacturer fared.

Mike Rockenfeller arrived as reigning champion and carried the number 1 on his Audi RS 5 DTM, now with Timo Scheider alongside him at Phoenix after a major reshuffle of Audi's drivers. BMW introduced the new M4 DTM with eight cars and two rookies, Maxime Martin and António Félix da Costa. Mercedes-Benz brought Paul di Resta back to the series, and Vitaly Petrov made his DTM debut. Seven past champions were on the grid. BMW had finished its pre-season preparation with a four-day test at Hockenheim, where Marco Wittmann was fastest on two of the four days. Marquardt said it was still hard to predict anything for the first weekend. Rockenfeller said he wanted to score plenty of points straight away.

chapters.title: Tambay takes a first pole as Mercedes sinks to the back
text: Adrien Tambay put his Abt Audi on pole with 1:32.272, the first of his DTM career, after he said he had come close to being eliminated in the first session, and he thanked mechanics who had barely slept for two nights. Wittmann was 0.147 seconds slower in the RMG BMW, and Bruno Spengler's Schnitzer BMW (1:32.600) was third. Félix da Costa had appeared at the top of the times in the closing minutes, but that lap was deleted because he ran wide at the first corner, and the Red Bull-liveried MTEK BMW rookie started fourth on 1:32.608.

Mattias Ekström lined up fifth on 1:32.624, with Edoardo Mortara sixth, Martin Tomczyk seventh, Timo Glock eighth and Scheider ninth. Rockenfeller, the champion, started tenth, with Farfus 11th, Hand 16th and Green 17th. Miguel Molina had set the sixth-fastest time but began the race 23rd, from the last place on the grid.

The session was a bad one for Mercedes-Benz. Gary Paffett and Pascal Wehrlein were the only Mercedes drivers to get through the first session, and they qualified 14th and 15th. Di Resta, Daniel Juncadella, Robert Wickens, Christian Vietoris and Petrov filled places 18 to 22, with Petrov last of the five on his qualifying debut. The two other rookies, Nico Müller and Martin, were 12th and 13th.

chapters.title: Wittmann passes Tambay, Green is out
text: The race was run in bright sunshine, with an air temperature of 13 degrees. Tambay led away from pole, but Wittmann was past him by the third lap at the latest and began to pull away on the option tyre. Behind them the field was split by tyre choice: most of the leaders started on options, while Ekström, Rockenfeller, Mortara, Spengler, Tomczyk and Farfus began on the standard compound and waited for the stops.

Jamie Green's Rosberg Audi was the first car out. He collided with Augusto Farfus in the opening laps and was in the garage after only two laps. At the other end of the order, Mercedes option starters Wickens and Vietoris moved into the top ten from the back of the grid, but both would fall away once the field had stopped.

chapters.title: Standard-tyre starters turn the race around
text: The single mandatory stop decided most of the order. Wittmann came in from the lead to take the standard tyre and came out still clear of Tambay, which effectively settled the race. The drivers who had started on the standard compound now held the advantage: they were on the faster option for the second half and attacked the cars that had run it first.

Ekström was the best example, running around eighth early on and then working his way forward position by position. Rockenfeller used the same plan to go from tenth on the grid to fourth. Glock, who had made up places on the first lap, took fifth. Wickens, on the other hand, fell back to 18th and Vietoris to 15th after their opening-stint gains.

chapters.title: Scheider is spun and Mortara loses a tyre
text: Scheider had been as high as third on the option strategy when Félix da Costa, who had been in reach of the podium for long periods, hit his Audi under the yellow flags late in the race and spun him. Da Costa was classified 21st, four laps down, and later apologised to Scheider and Audi. Scheider lost further places in a fight with Farfus on the last lap and finished ninth, one place behind the BMW.

Mortara, who was running ahead of Ekström on the same strategy, lost his chance with a front-left puncture on lap 31 and was classified 22nd, 11 laps down. With the Italian and the Phoenix car both delayed, Ekström had a clear run at Tambay and passed his fellow Audi driver in the closing laps to take second place.

chapters.title: Wittmann wins by 12.869 seconds
text: Wittmann crossed the line after 42 laps in 1:06:40.548, 12.869 seconds ahead of Ekström, who had started fifth on the standard tyre. Tambay held on to third, 14.879 seconds behind, from Rockenfeller, who was 17.593 seconds back. Glock was fifth ahead of Spengler, Tomczyk and Farfus, so that BMW had six of the top ten finishers. Scheider took ninth and Joey Hand, 16th on the grid, collected the last point in tenth.

Tomczyk set the fastest lap, a 1:32.532 on lap 25. Mercedes-Benz left the weekend without a point, as Wehrlein, 11th, was the best of their cars ahead of Paffett in 12th. Molina, from the back of the grid, climbed to 13th.

chapters.title: A first win for the M4 and the points lead for Wittmann
text: Wittmann took the first DTM victory of his career in the first race of the new BMW M4 DTM, a result that handed the Hockenheim opener to a car that had never raced before. He said he had checked his mirrors all afternoon, knew that the option-tyre runners would be quicker at the end, and that the gap he had built was big enough to hold. BMW's motorsport director Jens Marquardt described it as a dream debut weekend and credited the winter's work of Stefan Reinhold's RMG team. Behind him the BMW garage had mixed feelings: Spengler, who started third, was disappointed with sixth after Schnitzer chose to start both of its cars on the standard tyre, and Hand was pleased to have turned 16th on the grid into a point.

For Audi it was a strong day with a few frustrations. Ekström, Tambay and Rockenfeller took three of the top four places, and Tambay turned his first pole into a podium. Ekström said he could "live well with second place" but admitted that the BMWs had looked strong too, and Audi's head of DTM, Dieter Gass, said the result might have been better still had Scheider and Mortara not lost out. Molina, who started from the back of the grid, worked his way up to 13th. Audi reported 75,000 spectators over the weekend.

The day was a disappointment for Mercedes-Benz, which went home without a point. Wehrlein, the best-placed car in 11th, said that the weekend had been difficult and that the team would have to analyse everything to improve, with Paffett 12th, di Resta 14th and Vietoris 15th. The new rookies fared unevenly: Müller was 16th after dropping to the back at the start, Martin 20th after a pit-stop problem with a wheel that cost him a good result, and Félix da Costa blamed himself for the collision with Scheider that spoiled his strong first race.

In the drivers' standings Wittmann led with 25 points, ahead of Ekström on 18, Tambay on 15, Rockenfeller on 12, Glock on 10 and Spengler on eight. The second of the ten races followed two weeks later, on 18 May at the Motorsport Arena Oschersleben, where the performance weights of each brand's drivers would change depending on what its cars had achieved at Hockenheim.

facts.v: Marco Wittmann won the season opener, his first DTM victory, in the new BMW M4 DTM's first race.
